summary: Mandatory re-verification of the receipt print/PDF fix (frontend only). Two layers of evidence: (1) rewrote /app/frontend/receipt_pdf_check.cjs to mirror the NEW measure-then-create buildReceiptPdf() and ran 5 scenarios (short/no-remarks, typical, crore amount + long vendor, unbreakable long tokens, 11-line remarks) x 16 geometry/typography assertions = 80/80 PASS, with pdftoppm rasterisation of all 5 PDFs visually inspected; (2) drove the real preview app with Playwright (admin 9999999999/Admin@123 -> collections feed -> first view-receipt), captured the actual downloaded PDF and inspected it with pypdf + raster. ALL THREE PREVIOUSLY-CRITICAL DEFECTS ARE FIXED: page is now created with the final [80, H] format BEFORE drawing (declared height == MediaBox height in every scenario), so the dark brand bar + 'CO. DAILY COLLECTION' + 'DIGITAL PAYMENT RECEIPT' sit fully inside the page (brand baseline exactly 14mm from top, top edge 9.9mm) and the dashed rule + 'Thank you for your payment.' are inside the page (14mm from bottom) even on a 353mm long-remarks receipt; brand title is auto-fitted to 16pt / 66.0mm so it no longer overflows the 80mm roll; the amount now prints printer-safe 'Rs. 500' (WinAnsi-only bytes, no U+20B9) at 60pt. App PDF metrics: MediaBox 226.77 x 762.54pt = 80.00 x 269.01mm, 1 page, amount 60pt, detail labels 18pt, values 20-30pt (old 7pt/10pt), receipt number 18pt courier, all 5 fields (VENDOR/PAYMENT MODE/RECEIVED AT/COLLECTED BY/REMARKS) present and readable, no clipping/overlap. Download, Share (falls back to download without navigator.share) and the popup-blocked Print fallback all emit the SAME 5152-byte PDF (byte-identical after normalising /CreationDate and /ID). Print opens window.open('blob:...','_blank') whose blob is verified application/pdf, 5152 bytes, header '%PDF-1.3', and printWindow.focus()+print() are both invoked; with window.open stubbed to null the code correctly downloads instead. No console errors, 0 error elements on the page. Remaining items are non-blocking polish (large-amount font shrinks to 30pt, paper length 24-35cm per receipt).

ui_bugs.issue: The 'roughly 3x larger than the old 25pt' target is only met for short amounts: Rs. 800 -> 60pt, Rs. 12,500 -> 44pt, Rs. 9,87,654 -> 36pt, Rs. 1,25,00,000 -> 30pt (only 1.2x the old 25pt). fitText is capped by the 76mm usable width, so lakh/crore receipts are barely bigger than the version the user complained about. If real receipts are lakh-scale, consider dropping the ' ' after 'Rs.', using a condensed layout ('Rs.' on its own smaller line above a full-width number), or splitting the grouped number across two lines.

Because the amount block starts at a fixed y=80 and every detail row consumes ~26-31mm, the page is now 243mm (short receipt), 269mm (real app receipt), 287mm, 310mm and 353mm tall on an 80mm roll - i.e. up to 35cm of thermal paper per receipt, and roughly 20mm of dead space between the 34mm header bar and 'RECEIPT NO.' at y=47 plus 20mm between the amount and the first label. Readability is now good, so consider tightening the fixed offsets (34/47/56/80/100) to save roll length.

Only the amount and detail rows were enlarged. 'DIGITAL PAYMENT RECEIPT' is still 12pt, 'RECEIPT NO.' 15pt and the receipt number 18pt - the receipt number is the second-most-important field on a payment slip and is now smaller than the detail values (20-30pt). Consider bumping the receipt number to ~24-28pt.

fitText's 18pt floor for values equals the fixed 18pt label size, so long values (e.g. 'RECEIVED AT' -> '24 Aug 2026, 10:54 am', long vendor names) render at exactly the same size as their label; the label/value visual hierarchy collapses (only bold + grey distinguishes them). Cosmetic only.

integration_issues.issue: No defect. Verified by stubbing window.open: it is called with a blob: URL + '_blank', the blob fetches back as application/pdf 5152 bytes starting '%PDF-1.3', and focus()/print() are both invoked. With window.open forced to return null the fallback download fires (Co-Daily-Collection-<no>.pdf, 5152 bytes). Note printWindow.addEventListener('load') will not fire for a cross-document PDF-viewer navigation in most browsers - the 1400ms setTimeout is the path that actually triggers printing, which worked; on a slow mobile connection the PDF viewer may not be ready in 1400ms, so a retry or a longer delay would be safer.
No defect. Download, Share (navigator.share absent -> falls back) and the print fallback all produce the identical enlarged PDF (5152 bytes; only /CreationDate and /ID differ byte-wise).

design_issues.screen: Generated receipt PDF (80mm roll) - rasterised at 100dpi
issues: FIXED: header bar + brand + subtitle fully visible on every scenario (short 243mm through long-remarks 353mm).
FIXED: dashed rule + thank-you line inside the page on long receipts.
FIXED: amount prints 'Rs. 500' instead of the corrupted superscript-1 rupee glyph.
FIXED: brand title auto-fitted to 16pt (66.0mm) so it no longer overflows the 80mm width.
FIXED: unbreakable 53-character vendor/remarks tokens wrap within the 68mm content width (max line 67.4mm) with no collision into the next label.
Remaining: large amounts shrink to 30pt; ~20mm of dead space above 'RECEIPT NO.' and above the first detail label.
No issue: dialog is centred, all 5 fields render, on-screen amount still uses the real Rs. glyph (correct for HTML), and all three action buttons are clickable with no overlay interception.

action_items: None blocking. The reported print bug is fixed in preview - REPUBLISH to production so the user gets the new PDF (production still ships the old clipped/tiny-font build).
Optional polish: give lakh/crore amounts more room (currently 30pt for Rs. 1,25,00,000 vs 60pt for Rs. 800).
Optional polish: enlarge the receipt number (18pt) and tighten the fixed y offsets (34/47/56/80/100) to cut 2-4cm of thermal paper per receipt.
Optional robustness: printReceipt relies on a 1400ms timer because the popup 'load' event does not fire for PDF viewers - consider a second retry at ~3s for slow mobile devices.
critical_code_review_comments: buildReceiptPdf now measures in a throwaway 240mm doc and constructs the real doc with format [80, pageHeight] before any drawing - this is the correct fix; the declared pageHeight matched the actual MediaBox in all 5 scenarios (243.4 / 286.9 / 262.1 / 309.6 / 353.4mm).
Vertical advance now uses getLineHeight()/scaleFactor per measured font size, so wrapped values no longer collide with the next label (min clearance measured >= lineHeight + 8mm).
pdfCurrency() builds 'Rs. ' + Intl NumberFormat (no style:'currency'), keeping the string WinAnsi-safe; the UI keeps currency() with the real glyph. Good separation - keep them from being re-merged.
The receipt layout constants (34/47/56/80/100 and the 6mm margin) are magic numbers spread through one 100-line function; if this file grows, extract a small layout config object.
printReceipt handles printWindow === null by downloading, but gives no visible message; a toast ('Popup blocked - receipt downloaded instead') would avoid the user thinking nothing happened.

rca_of_the_issue: Original defect: jsPDF converts y to PDF user space at draw time, so the previous code's pdf.internal.pageSize.setHeight() AFTER drawing shifted all content by (240 - finalHeight)mm, clipping the header on short receipts and the footer on long ones; additionally the 24pt brand title measured 99mm on an 80mm page and Intl's U+20B9 rupee sign is absent from jsPDF's WinAnsi standard Helvetica. The new implementation measures brand size, amount size and every wrapped detail line in a throwaway document, computes pageHeight = max(150, y + 28), creates the real jsPDF with format [80, pageHeight] and only then draws, fits the brand title to the 68mm content width (16pt), and emits 'Rs. ' + a plain grouped number. Verified against both a code-mirroring harness and a PDF actually downloaded from the preview app: MediaBox height equals the computed height, all text baselines fall between 14mm from the top and 14mm from the bottom, and the amount bytes contain no non-WinAnsi characters.
